context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to approve, decline, or flag suspicious transactions while managing analyst reviews. It operates within strict compliance and budgetary constraints to ensure secure, low-latency financial transaction processing.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Merchants (API Client)
- Fraud Analyst & Risk/Compliance Officer
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (AWS-hosted)
- Card Tokenization Vault (External Service)
- Identity Provider (AWS IAM / Cognito)
- Immutable Audit Sink (AWS S3 Object Lock)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to System: Sends authorization requests via gRPC and HTTPS using TLS 1.3 with mTLS.
- System to Card Tokenization Vault: Interfaced via outbound HTTPS APIs for tokenized data validation.
- System to AWS S3 Object Lock: Ingests decision inputs, model versions, and explanations into WORM storage using AWS KMS CMK encryption.
- System to Amazon CloudWatch & Route 53: Emits real-time health metrics and heartbeats for boundary monitoring.

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Infrastructure: AWS (`eu-west-1` region) chosen to leverage managed services within the €25,000/month budget.
- Security & Authentication: TLS 1.3 with mTLS, AES-256 encryption, and AWS IAM / Cognito for Role-Based Access Control.
- Audit & Storage: AWS S3 Object Lock configured for WORM compliance to retain immutable records for 7 years.
- Observability: Amazon CloudWatch and AWS Route 53 health checks for sub-second telemetry and boundary monitoring.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and tamper-evident 7-year auditability while minimizing operational overhead for a three-engineer team. Bounding the system scope and offloading edge fail-safes to upstream gateways ensures sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within a fixed monthly budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud before approval and provides case management for suspicious payment reviews. Built for a mid-size payment processor, it meets strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance requirements within a fixed budget and small engineering team.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst & Risk/Compliance Officer
* Merchant / Operations Manager & System Integrator (Payment Gateway)
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go on Amazon ECS Fargate)
* Case Management App (Node.js/TypeScript on Amazon ECS Fargate)
* Feature Store & Cache (Amazon ElastiCache Redis)
* Database (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2)
* Messaging & Audit Pipeline (Amazon SQS/SNS and Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
* Model Registry (Amazon SageMaker Model Registry)
* Network & Security (AWS WAF, Amazon API Gateway, Route 53, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS KMS)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway invokes Real-Time Scoring Engine via HTTPS/REST with mTLS over Amazon API Gateway
* Scoring Engine reads features from Amazon ElastiCache Redis
* Scoring Engine publishes asynchronous events to Amazon SQS
* SQS writes compliance audit logs to Amazon S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) using AWS KMS keys
* Fraud Analysts access Case Management App via HTTPS over Amazon API Gateway
* Case Management App reads/writes relational case data to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2
* Route 53 and API Gateway provide circuit-breaker fallback mechanisms for R-07 fail-safe requirements

## Technology Stack
* Compute: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate using Go and Node.js/TypeScript for predictable latency and zero cold starts
* Storage & Caching: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 for relational scaling; Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for sub-millisecond feature lookups
* Compliance & Audit: Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS for tamper-evident 7-year audit storage
* Messaging: Amazon SQS/SNS for decoupled, serverless asynchronous processing
* Security & Routing: AWS WAF, API Gateway, AWS Secrets Manager, and Route 53 for mTLS, credential rotation, and fail-safe routing

## Rationale
The serverless-adjacent container architecture maximizes managed AWS services to minimize operational toil for a 3-engineer team while strictly maintaining the 25k EUR monthly budget. Go on ECS Fargate combined with Redis caching guarantees sub-50ms P99 decision latency at 3,000 TPS, while S3 Object Lock and SQS ensure PCI-DSS compliance and tamper-evident auditability.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under strict latency and compliance constraints. It evaluates transactions before approval and routes suspicious payments to fraud analysts for case management.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go on Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Case Management App (Node.js/TypeScript on Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Feature Store & Cache (Amazon ElastiCache Redis)
- Database (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2)
- Model Registry (Amazon SageMaker Model Registry)
- Messaging & Audit Pipeline (Amazon SQS/SNS and Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
- Network & Security (AWS WAF, Amazon API Gateway, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS KMS, AWS X-Ray)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Merchants -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Invokes authorization scoring requests via HTTPS/REST with mTLS [Amazon API Gateway]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Feature Store & Cache: Reads low-latency features [Amazon ElastiCache Redis]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Messaging & Audit Pipeline: Publishes compliance audit events [Amazon SQS/SNS and Amazon S3]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Model Registry: Retrieves cryptographically signed models [Amazon SageMaker]

## Technology Stack
- Go (net/http, ONNX Runtime): Delivers sub-50ms P99 latency and high throughput for the scoring engine
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Provides serverless container orchestration manageable by a 3-engineer team
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Delivers ultra-low latency feature retrieval
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year auditable storage for PCI-DSS compliance

## Rationale
This architecture combines Go and ECS Fargate to easily meet the 3,000 TPS and <50ms P99 latency requirements within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It strictly isolates sensitive payment data to maintain PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while providing zero-downtime model updates.

Case Management App.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening is a low-latency financial system that screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst review workflows. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year auditability on AWS with a 3-engineer team.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk/Compliance Officer
- Case Management App (Node.js/TypeScript on Amazon ECS Fargate)
- API Controller Component, Case Service Component, Audit Client Component, Data Repository Component, Dashboard & Metrics Component
- Amazon API Gateway
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2
- Immutable Audit Sink (Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
- Identity Provider

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst & Risk/Compliance Officer -> Amazon API Gateway: Accesses case management UI [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Amazon API Gateway -> API Controller Component: Routes authenticated API requests [HTTP / JSON]
- Case Service Component -> Data Repository Component: Reads and writes relational case state [TypeORM / Prisma]
- Data Repository Component -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Persists case data [IAM DB Auth / TLS]
- Audit Client Component -> Immutable Audit Sink: Emits cryptographically signed case resolution events [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Case Management App -> Identity Provider: Validates OIDC/OAuth2 tokens and RBAC claims [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Runtime: Node.js and TypeScript on Amazon ECS Fargate for lightweight, ephemeral, and stateless container management.
- Backend Framework: Express.js/Fastify for simple routing without heavy CQRS overhead.
- Database ORM: TypeORM/Prisma for type-safe relational data mapping.
- Storage & Audit: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 and Amazon S3 with Object Lock for immutable 7-year audit logging.
- Security & Auth: AWS KMS, AWS IAM, and OIDC/OAuth2 via Identity Provider for secretless infrastructure and strict RBAC.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Modular component boundaries in Node.js ensure maintainability while meeting strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security and tamper-evident audit requirements.

Feature Store & Cache.analysis:
## Overview
The Feature Store & Cache provides sub-millisecond feature lookups for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It maintains aggregated user and card behavioral data to ensure high-performance fraud scoring.

## Key Elements
- Feature Retrieval API / Client Layer
- In-Memory Cache & Store
- Feature Ingestion Worker
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis (Standard Tier)

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Feature Retrieval API / Client Layer: Reads features via RESP over TCP (with TLS 1.3)
- Feature Ingestion Worker -> In-Memory Cache & Store: Writes feature updates asynchronously via Redis commands over TLS
- Feature Store & Cache -> AWS Secrets Manager: Fetches authentication tokens via AWS SDK (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Chosen for sub-millisecond latency and high throughput within budget
- Redis ACLs: Enforces least-privilege read/write separation between services
- AWS KMS & TLS 1.3: Secures data at rest and in transit for PCI-DSS compliance

## Rationale
This architecture delivers P99 decision latency under 50 ms while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It operates efficiently within budget limits for a lean engineering team.

## Overview
Real-time payment fraud screening system processing card-not-present transactions for a mid-size payment processor. It provides sub-50ms fraud scoring and case management while ensuring strict compliance, auditability, and cost efficiency.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk/Compliance Officer (Users)
- Payment Gateway / Merchants & Card Tokenization Vault (External Systems)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go on Amazon ECS Fargate container)
- Case Management App (Node.js/TypeScript on Amazon ECS Fargate container)
- Messaging & Audit Pipeline (Amazon SQS and Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
- Feature Store & Cache (Amazon ElastiCache Redis)
- Database (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2)
- Model Registry (Amazon SageMaker Model Registry)
- Network & Security (AWS WAF, Amazon API Gateway, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS KMS)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> API Gateway: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Messaging & Audit Pipeline: Publishes asynchronous events and logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS over VPC Endpoints]
- Messaging & Audit Pipeline -> Immutable Audit Sink: Writes tamper-evident logs [Amazon S3 Object Lock Compliance Mode and AWS KMS]
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management App: Reviews flagged transactions [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Compute: Amazon ECS Fargate (Go for scoring/workers, Node.js/TypeScript for case management) for predictable resource usage and zero Lambda cold starts
- Storage & Caching: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 and Amazon ElastiCache Redis for relational data and low-latency feature retrieval
- Messaging & Audit: Amazon SQS and Amazon S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) using AWS KMS for 7-year tamper-evident audit logs
- Lifecycle Management: Amazon S3 Lifecycle Policies transitioning to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days to meet budget constraints

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless containers and managed AWS services to guarantee P99 latency under 50 ms at 3,000 TPS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability via S3 Object Lock and AWS KMS while remaining maintainable for a three-person engineering team.

Network & Security.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture defines a real-time payment fraud screening system for processing card-not-present authorizations securely. It provides automated scoring, case management for analysts, and tamper-evident auditing within strict budget and compliance limits.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts & Risk/Compliance Officers (Users)
- Payment Gateway / Merchants & Card Tokenization Vault (External Systems)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine & Case Management App (Containers on ECS Fargate)
- Feature Store & Cache (Amazon ElastiCache Redis) & Database (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)
- Network & Security (AWS WAF, Amazon API Gateway, AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateways to API Gateway via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- API Gateway to ECS Fargate tasks via VPC Links using internal HTTPS
- ECS Fargate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and ElastiCache Redis via TCP/TLS
- Secrets Manager and KMS to ECS Fargate via AWS IAM

## Technology Stack
- Amazon API Gateway & AWS WAF: Edge routing and request filtering for high-throughput traffic
- AWS KMS & AWS Secrets Manager: Encryption, key segregation, and automated credential rotation for PCI-DSS compliance
- AWS VPC Security Groups: Micro-segmentation ensuring strict network isolation
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Serverless container orchestration aligned with a 3-engineer team constraint

## Rationale
Managed AWS services minimize operational toil for a small three-engineer team while keeping infrastructure costs well within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Enforcing strict network isolation, encryption in transit, and KMS key segregation satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year audit requirements without exceeding the 50 ms P99 latency threshold.
